about.text: Cheese that keeps much of its water, more than 67 % in the cheese without its fat under German cheese law, so that it stays soft and, as it ripens from the outside in, turns creamy. In Germany called Weichkäse; the bloomy and washed rinds are soft cheeses taken further.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: The curd drains under its own weight instead of being pressed, so it keeps a lot of water: soft cheese has more than 67 % moisture in the fat-free mass under both Codex and German law. That moist paste ripens quickly and stays spoonable or spreadable.
